issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a measurement function named dd_measure_all, but the template defines the function as measure_all_dd (name swapped). This is both an inner-template inconsistency (template docstring/listing refers to dd_measure_all, but the actual function implemented is measure_all_dd) and a cross-artifact mismatch (students following the template will implement/see measure_all_dd while tests and the solution expect dd_measure_all). This mismatch will cause confusion and test failures because the expected function name (dd_measure_all) is absent from the template API.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template API match the problem statement and solution by renaming the template function measure_all_dd to dd_measure_all (and update any internal references). Alternatively, provide a thin wrapper in the template: define dd_measure_all(...) that calls measure_all_dd(...). Also ensure the top-level docstring and any references consistently use dd_measure_all.

issues.description: The decision-diagram measurement routine is named inconsistently between artifacts. The problem statement (and the solution) expect a function named `dd_measure_all`, but the template repository provides a function stub named `measure_all_dd`. This swaps the token order (and omits the `dd_` prefix convention used elsewhere) and may prevent students from finding/implementing the expected function or from mapping the task description to the template code. It also creates potential confusion with the tensor-network measurement function `measure_all` (no `dd_` prefix).
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the template stub `measure_all_dd` to `dd_measure_all` (and update any internal references) so the template, problem statement, and solution consistently use `dd_measure_all`. Preserve the `dd_` prefix to clearly distinguish decision-diagram measurement (`dd_measure_all`) from the tensor-network measurement (`measure_all`).
